analysis: Dallas lost WR1 CeeDee Lamb (high-ankle sprain) and rookie guard Tyler Booker for this one, while Green Bay is missing both interior DTs (Javon Hargrave, Jonathan Ford -- triggering the model's depth-stacking penalty) plus a starting corner. The sim's adjusted total dropped from an injury-blind 47.8 to 41.9, well under the market's 53.5 -- a near-12-point gap that is unusually wide even accounting for the model still carrying some 2025-weighted scoring averages this early in the season.

Both offenses took real hits: Dallas without its top target, Green Bay's pass rush and secondary both thinned out which could actually push the OTHER way on pace/scoring if Dallas's backup WRs find room against a weakened GB secondary -- the under lean here is real but not a blowout-confidence lean given how much roster uncertainty is stacked on both sides.
